subject: Routing policy lab: POC kickoff scheduling and reschedule
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-retail.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC kickoff — routing policy lab (proposed windows)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited to move to a hands-on POC. We'd like to schedule a kickoff + working session focused on routing policy: model selection, fallback rules, regional routing, and tiering.

Two windows that work for our engineering/product leads (PST):
- Tuesday Nov 10, 10:00–12:00 PST (2 hr lab: prompt review + routing config)
- Wednesday Nov 11, 13:00–15:00 PST (2 hr lab: load tests + failover drills)

Attendees: me (Acme PM), Michael Torres (SRE), Priya Singh (ML infra). We may also loop in James from CloudPartner.

Can you confirm which slot works for Redwood and whether you want any pre-reads? Also if you prefer splitting into two shorter sessions, say 90m + 60m, we can be flexible.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Senior Product Manager, Acme Retail
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, James Li <james.li@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — routing policy lab (proposed windows)

Elena — appreciate the clarity. Both windows work in principle; kicking off with a single 2-hr hands-on lab should be fine. Proposed plan:

Option A (preferred): Tue Nov 10, 10:00–12:00 PST
- 10:00–10:20: introductions, objectives, success criteria
- 10:20–11:15: prompt review & model selection (end-to-end prompts, quality targets)
- 11:15–11:45: routing policy config (fallbacks, region pinning, tiering rules)
- 11:45–12:00: next steps + action items

Option B (fallback): Wed Nov 11, 13:00–15:00 PST — we can shift the load-tests to a separate 60m follow-up if you prefer.

Prep requests: if you can share a 10–15 prompt sample (or a small dataset) and the rough traffic profile (p95 latency target, tokens/sec, expected concurrency), that will let us configure sensible batch/quantization and routing tiers ahead of time. I added Jordan (routing lead) and Stephanie (solutions) on cc to coordinate capacity.

I'll block Option A tentatively on our calendars and send a formal invite once we hear from your team.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-retail.com>, James Li <james.li@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — routing policy lab (proposed windows)

Quick note from routing team: Tue Nov 10 at 10:00 works for us. One ask — if Acme can share a short list (<=100) of representative prompts and an estimated QPS profile (even ballpark), we'll bring a pre-configured routing policy and a candidate fallback model so the hands-on time is spent tuning rather than building from scratch.

Also flag: for the load test portion we'll need a 30–45 minute window where we can drive synthetic traffic at the requested concurrency; please confirm whether that should run against your test environment or against our sandbox (we can do either).

— Jordan
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-retail.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, James Li <james.li@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — routing policy lab (proposed windows)

Hi all — small schedule conflict on our side. Can we shift to Nov 12 instead? Our SRE is out on 11th. New options:
- Fri Nov 12, 09:30–11:30 PST (preferred)
- Fri Nov 12, 15:00–17:00 PST (backup)

We will upload a 50-row sample_prompts.csv to the drive by EOD Thu so you can review. For load tests, we'd prefer Redwood sandbox to avoid touching production.

Apologies for the churn — hoping Nov 12 works.

Thanks,
Elena

Elena — Nov 12 09:30–11:30 PST works for the team. Confirming details and prep below:

Final time: Fri, Nov 12, 09:30–11:30 PST (90–120m hands-on lab)
Attendees (confirmed): Elena Park (Acme PM), Michael Torres (Acme SRE), Priya Singh (Acme ML), James Li (CloudPartner), Jonas Weber (Redwood), Jordan Blake (Redwood), Stephanie Nguyen (Redwood)

Action items / prep (Acme):
- Upload sample_prompts.csv (you mentioned 50 rows) — thanks, we'll use to pre-seed prompt templates
- Share estimated peak concurrency and p95 latency target (ballpark fine)
- Indicate whether there are any region-specific constraints (EU/CA data regions, etc.) — we assume US by default

Redwood will deliver before the session:
- POC_Agenda_v3.pdf (attached) — includes timing and roles
- sample_prompts.csv (sanity-checked) — attached as example formatting
- Calendar invite (sent) and a shared drive with the pre-reads: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-poc-routing-prep

Load tests: we will run synthetic load from our sandbox unless you prefer otherwise — sounds like sandbox is preferred. We'll coordinate the exact 30–45m test window during the session.

I've attached the agenda and a small CSV template for prompts. Please accept the calendar invite (you should have received it from calendar@redwood.ai). If anything else changes, ping me. Looking forward to it.

Attachments: POC_Agenda_v3.pdf (2 pages), sample_prompts.csv (50 rows)

— Jonas
